updates.title: AWS makes SageMaker AI training sessions generally available
updates.whatChanged: AWS made SageMaker AI training sessions generally available on 22 October. Stateful, serverless GPU sessions expose sampling, gradient and optimizer calls for custom supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement-learning loops. AWS manages GPU allocation, distributed execution, fault recovery and checkpoints for four supported models.
updates.whyCare: You can run custom loss functions, reward signals and multi-turn reinforcement-learning loops without operating GPU clusters. Check supported models and Regions before moving an experiment.
updates.before: Teams used predefined SageMaker customization recipes or managed their own GPU clusters for custom training loops.
updates.after: Teams can compose stateful SageMaker AI session calls for sampling, gradient updates and optimization. AWS allocates GPUs and manages distributed execution, fault recovery and checkpoints.
updates.learn: Check supported models and Regions. Compare per-token charges with GPU job costs. Test recovery, checkpointing and model quality on your reward loop.

sources.name: AWS Machine Learning Blog - Announcing new ways to customize models with SageMaker AI, without managing GPUs

updates.architectureImplication: Keep reward logic, evaluation and loop control in your code. Call SageMaker AI for GPU-backed sampling and weight updates. Validate data movement, session quotas and cost against self-managed training jobs.
